title: Turandot
facts: Turandot premiered at La Scala on 25 April 1926, about a year and a half after Puccini’s death; Franco Alfano completed the music.
Diagnosed with throat cancer, Puccini begged Toscanini before leaving for treatment: “Don’t let my Turandot die.”
Liù’s death and funeral procession were the last music Puccini composed and orchestrated. He left 36 pages of sketches for the ending.
At the premiere Toscanini stopped here and told the audience: “Here the opera ends, because at this point the maestro died.” The curtain came down.
Toscanini and Ricordi criticized Alfano’s first ending so severely that he had to write a second, strictly censored version, which Toscanini then cut by about three minutes.
Rosa Raisa, the first Turandot, said neither Puccini nor Toscanini ever pronounced the final “t” of the name.
It was Schiller’s version of the tale that inspired Puccini to write the opera.
Pavarotti took “Nessun dorma” far beyond the opera world with his performance for the 1990 World Cup; his single reached number 2 in the UK.
The Three Tenors sang “Nessun dorma” at three more World Cup finals: 1994, 1998 and 2002.
For many years China forbade performances of Turandot, saying it portrayed the country unfavourably.
Critic Joseph Kerman: “Puccini, however, did not find it; his music does nothing to rationalise the legend or illuminate the characters.”
“Del primo pianto” was sung at the premiere but cut from the first complete recording. It was later restored to most performances.
Luciano Berio wrote a new completion in 2002, with the cooperation of the publisher, Ricordi.
